headline: Funding flows. Satellites launch. Budgets grow.
deck: This week saw significant funding rounds and strategic launches, underscoring the industry's relentless pace.

stories.head: Apex's valuation skyrockets after $200 million raise
stories.body: Apex has raised $200 million, boosting its valuation to $2.3 billion as it focuses on productized satellite buses. This funding is a clear signal that investors are still keen on satellite technology, even as the market matures. The company’s next-gen Aries platform is expected to be a key player in upcoming contracts.
stories.soWhat: In a sector where hype often overshadows substance, Apex's valuation suggests that tangible products still drive investor confidence.

stories.head: Ariane 6 to debut with Amazon's satellite fleet
stories.body: The first Ariane 6 launch will carry 36 Amazon Leo satellites, showcasing the upgraded boosters designed to enhance payload capacity. This launch is a critical step for Amazon as it aims to establish a foothold in the competitive broadband space market. With this mission, ArianeGroup is also betting on its technical upgrades to regain market share.
stories.soWhat: Ariane 6’s performance will be closely monitored; a successful launch could breathe new life into Europe's launch capabilities, while a failure could deepen its woes.

stories.head: Palantir secures $480 million extension for TITAN
stories.body: Palantir has won a $480 million extension for its TITAN ground station program, demonstrating the company's persistent grip on government contracts. This extension underscores the importance of robust data management systems in defense operations, particularly as the military seeks to integrate more advanced technologies. The funding reflects a growing recognition of the need for data-driven decision-making in defense.
stories.soWhat: In an era of tightening budgets, Palantir's ability to secure extensions indicates that the government is prioritizing proven capabilities over new entrants.

watchlist.title: True Anomaly's Series C impacts defense tech
watchlist.body: True Anomaly's $190 million Series C could signal a shift in co-orbital security investments, especially as the DoD emphasizes space domain awareness.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser moves closer to launch
watchlist.body: With the Dream Chaser DoD variant passing its critical design review, the focus will be on whether it can meet the ambitious timelines set for its first orbital flight.

watchlist.title: Anduril and L3Harris partnership to watch
watchlist.body: Their tactical SDA constellation bid may reshape how defense contracts are awarded, especially as collaboration becomes essential in complex projects.

watchlist.title: FY27 budget implications for space resilience
watchlist.body: The $1.4 billion boost for space resilience in the FY27 budget could lead to increased opportunities for contractors focused on security and surveillance technologies.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
